clusters.name: Walter's move to Sorrel Valley, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter moving the family across the country to buy an apple orchard in March 1952, within the year: June homesick and writing to her sister daily, Walter out in the trees and distant from June, Glen in fights at school, Walter cutting off from his brother Harlan, June keeping to bed for weeks, Walter and June rowing over money for trees, and June joining the church choir as her letters thinned out. Her functioning and anxiety shifted as she found footing in the new place by autumn.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failing, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard failing in May 1968 when the late frost took the whole crop and the bank called in the loan: Walter drinking heavily most nights, Walter and Glen blaming each other over the loan, Glen and Marian taking over the family's money and talks with the bank, Carl's asthma attacks worsening that winter, you wetting the bed again in spring, and Walter stopping drinking by autumn and taking work pruning trees. The shifts pile up around the sale and the family's move to Ridgeport in October, with your symptom lasting into spring.

clusters.name: Glen's job loss at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen losing his job when the Ridgeport cannery closed in February 1975: Glen out of work most of that year and sitting in the truck for hours, loud fights between Glen and Marian at night over money, Marian taking a second job cleaning offices at night, you stopping eating properly and losing weight that summer, you keeping to your room and distant from Marian, Walter drinking again after six years off it in December, and you eating again and making the track team by June 1976. All the shifts are yours and those closest to you; no one else's shows in these months.

clusters.name: Wilma moving into your house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma selling her farm and moving into your house in January 1990: you clashed with Wilma over the children's bedtimes and meals, you working late and keeping out of the kitchen rows while Hollis took his mother's side, Owen having tantrums at preschool, Wilma taking over Lily's care, you developing eczema flaring on both hands, you and Hollis rowing most nights, and the eczema clearing over the summer after Wilma took a flat in town in June 1991. The shifts in your symptoms and your relationship moves pass from the household tension to you directly.

This is a short reaction to a real threat, not a period.

There is not enough to say what opened this.
